text: Paris was under siege and starving. <break time="0.8s" /> And one bright January morning. <break time="0.8s" /> Monsieur Morissot was walking sadly. <break time="0.8s" /> Along the boulevard. <break time="0.8s" /> With an empty stomach. <break time="0.8s" /> A watchmaker with nothing to do in wartime. <break time="0.8s" /> He walked on slowly. <break time="0.8s" /> His hands deep. <break time="0.8s" /> In the pockets of his uniform trousers. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly he stopped. <break time="0.8s" /> In front of a man. <break time="0.8s" /> Whom he recognized at once. <break time="0.8s" /> For it was Monsieur Sauvage. <break time="0.8s" /> His old friend from the riverside. <break time="0.8s" /> Before the war. <break time="0.8s" /> Morissot had left home. <break time="0.8s" /> At dawn every Sunday. <break time="0.8s" /> With a bamboo rod in his hand. <break time="0.8s" /> And a tin box on his back. <break time="0.8s" /> He took the train to Colombes. <break time="0.8s" /> And walked to the little island of Marante. <break time="0.8s" /> Where he would happily fish until night. <break time="0.8s" /> Every Sunday he met there. <break time="0.8s" /> A stout, cheerful little man. <break time="0.8s" /> Monsieur Sauvage. <break time="0.8s" /> Who sold cloth. <break time="0.8s" /> In a shop in Paris. <break time="0.8s" /> They often spent half the day. <break time="0.8s" /> Side by side. <break time="0.8s" /> Rod in hand. <break time="0.8s" /> And feet hanging over the water. <break time="0.8s" /> And they became close friends. <break time="0.8s" /> On some days. <break time="0.8s" /> They did not speak at all. <break time="0.8s" /> For they understood each other perfectly. <break time="0.8s" /> Without words. <break time="0.8s" /> Having the same simple tastes. <break time="0.8s" /> On spring mornings. <break time="0.8s" /> With the warm sun on their backs. <break time="0.8s" /> Morissot would say. <break time="0.8s" /> How pleasant this is and Sauvage would answer. <break time="0.8s" /> I know nothing better.
